documentTitle: Arrival Wave Scheduling, Gate Throughput & Queue Holding Principles

sections.sectionTitle: Balancing Gate Processing Rates Against Peak Arrival Waves
sections.summary: When peak arrival rates exceed combined entry gate and security checkpoint throughput, residual queues accumulate exponentially across consecutive intervals unless waves are staggered or gates added.
sections.verbatimQuote: If interval arrival demand exceeds aggregate gate and screening service rate, residual queue backlog compounds across subsequent intervals until either additional processing lanes open or arrival waves are staggered.

sections.sectionTitle: Sizing Holding Areas & Detecting Spillback Deficit
sections.summary: Compare cumulative peak queue length against reviewed holding-zone area capacity so overflow is mitigated before crowds back up onto public roadways or cross main exits.
sections.verbatimQuote: Designated security and entry holding zones must accommodate peak projected queue volume at reviewed queue densities; any holding-area deficit risks uncontrolled spillback onto external approaches.

sections.sectionTitle: Security Checkpoint & Ticket Scan Funnel Staging
sections.summary: Place ticket/pass verification upstream of high-density gathering zones with sufficient setback distance so queuing visitors remain in buffered lanes.
sections.verbatimQuote: Security screening and pass-verification lanes require adequate setback from gathering zones and multi-lane parallel fanning to prevent single-file choke delays.

sections.summary: Monitor high-affinity attraction zones near stages using secondary barrier pens, side relief aisles, and early staff interventions before local density escalates.
sections.verbatimQuote: High-affinity stage fronts require lateral relief exits, compartmentalized barrier pens for large audiences, and separation of wet utility points from stage electrical zones.

sections.summary: Event attendance ceilings are governed by the tightest constraint among usable standing space, ingress/egress flow, holding-buffer capacity, and statutory permit limits—never gross site area alone.
sections.verbatimQuote: Preliminary venue capacity is bounded by the tightest constraint among net standing space, gate ingress/egress flow, holding buffer capacity, and statutory permit caps, subject to documented human safety review.
